title: Select a store from the protected operation
description: Choose a workload to reveal the access path, the data model that makes it natural, and the guarantee that must remain explicit.

nodes.label: Application request
nodes.detail: Starts the operation. The design question is which fact this request must read or change correctly before the application returns a result.

nodes.label: Decision service
nodes.detail: Validates input, enforces application rules, and selects the authoritative path. It should not promote a cache or a derived view into the final source of truth for a critical write.

nodes.label: Relational database
nodes.detail: Protects related records with transactions, unique keys, foreign keys, and conditional writes. It is a strong starting point for authoritative business state.

nodes.label: Document database
nodes.detail: Stores fields normally read and updated together as one flexible record. Canonical ownership and cross-document consistency rules still need to be named.

nodes.label: Wide-column store
nodes.detail: Serves a known, partitioned query shape at high write volume. The partition key, retention policy, and allowed query windows are part of the data model.

nodes.label: Key-value store
nodes.detail: Returns a bounded value by a known identifier with predictable latency. It suits sessions and caches when expiry and rebuild behavior are safe.

scenarios.label: Seat reservation
scenarios.summary: Two customers can try to reserve the last seat at the same time. The application must accept at most one reservation and report a clear result to the other customer.
scenarios.result: Use a relational transaction or guarded conditional write around the seat invariant. Scale and schema are secondary to preventing two successful sales of one seat.

scenarios.label: Catalog listing
scenarios.summary: A product page has a variable set of attributes and is normally fetched as one object. Some fields vary by category and are added over time.
scenarios.result: A document is a natural starting model for the aggregate. Do not let copies of price, SKU, or inventory become independent writers when those values have a stricter owner elsewhere.

scenarios.label: Device telemetry
scenarios.summary: Devices append timestamped measurements continuously. Queries are known in advance: read one device or tenant over a bounded time window and expire old data.
scenarios.result: A wide-column model can make the known write and time-window read efficient when partition keys prevent hotspots. It is not a substitute for arbitrary ad hoc joins across every device.

scenarios.label: Session lookup
scenarios.summary: Each request includes a session ID and needs a small record quickly. The session expires and can be recreated from authoritative account state when appropriate.
scenarios.result: A key-value store with a TTL fits this known-key, bounded-state lookup. Keep billing, entitlement, and audit facts in durable authoritative storage if losing the session record would change the business outcome.
